claim: EG-2's byte-identity leg is a tautology: it compares a computation against itself, so its Alternate path (fall back to n sequential POSTs) can never be triggered, and DR47-6 is therefore ungated.
evidence: DR47-6 defines the fold as moveAdjacent applied n times to an accumulating buffer inside prepare. EG-2's evidence method imports the shipped moveAdjacent and asserts the fold equals the composition. moveAdjacent re-parses on every call (moduleContext(source) is its first statement), so the fold and the n-fold composition are the SAME sequence of calls on the same bytes. Both sides execute identical code; the equality holds by construction, not by measurement. The planted one-byte perturbation proves the comparator works, not that the arms can diverge. Acceptance 21 then promotes this to a permanent unit gate that cannot go RED.
impact: The decision the phase's undo semantics rest on (one drag, one journal entry) is approved on a probe that cannot fail. If in-memory folding and sequential server round-trips do diverge — the round-trip re-reads from disk, re-derives the expect baseline under deriveStructuralBaseline, and runs a full commitWrite CAS per step, none of which the in-memory fold does — the plan discovers it in S47-4 after the write is wired, past the story boundary DR47-10 exists to protect.
required_correction: Restate EG-2's claim and method so the two arms run different code paths: (arm A) one folded request through handleStructureEdit's prepare, versus (arm B) n sequential structure POSTs through the shipped single-step path, each with its own commitWrite, disk read-back and re-derived expect — compared on the final page.tsx bytes. Restate Pass/Alternate against that comparison, and restate acceptance 21 as that gate with an explicit RED-when mutation that makes it fail.

claim: DR47-1's first RED-when leg and pre-mortem S1's 'Residual: None' rest on a gate that cannot go RED under the mutation they name: the defaultPrevented triple in e2e/spacing-gesture.spec.ts does not change when the reorder-arming call is moved above ROW P.
evidence: In use-canvas-selection-shield.ts's onPointerSuppress, defaultPrevented on the popup-input row is false precisely because ROW P returns before suppressShieldPointer(e), which is the only call that invokes preventDefault() on that arm. DR47-1 specifies the reorder-arming call as a statement that arms a gesture; it does not call preventDefault(). Moving it above ROW P therefore leaves ROW P's early return intact and the popup input still reads defaultPrevented === false. The plan's leg table nonetheless states the mutation's effect as 'the popup input's press reads true'.
impact: The highest-risk edit in the phase (S47-2, on the file whose own docblock records the closest/matches regression that made a whole shipped row unreachable while every behavioural row stayed green) is protected by a leg that reports green under the exact misplacement it claims to catch. A lane that drives that triple, sees green under the mutation, and reads the green as confirmation repeats this file's recorded failure mode.
required_correction: Replace the first leg's RED-when with one that can fire. State acceptance 2 and 3 as arming assertions — a press on a data-dsh-handle target arms zero reorder gestures; a press on the spacing popup's input arms zero reorder gestures — each with its own RED-when (move the arming call above ROW D; above ROW P). Correct the leg table and S1, and drop the claim that the shipped defaultPrevented pair discriminates arming-call placement. If the reorder arm is intended to call preventDefault() too, say so in DR47-1 and re-derive acceptance 3, with its own argument for the change to ROW P's contract.

claim: No gate asserts that a committed reorder drag lands the element in the slot the blue line promised, and the DOM-slot to step-count mapping DR47-6 depends on is unsound in a case the plan does not name: an op-unit that renders no DOM node produces a successful 200 with zero visual movement.
evidence: DR47-7's predicate reads only the parent's computed display, the rendered children's rects, and their order — it is blind to source children that render nothing. adjacentOpUnit admits a JSXExpressionContainer whose expression is cond && <El/> as a full op-unit via opUnitElement, and oidOrNull reads the oid regardless of whether cond evaluated true. With {false && <X data-oid=.../>} between two rendered siblings the DOM slot list has 2 entries and the source op-unit list has 3: a one-slot drag computes n = 1, the fold swaps the target with the invisible container, commitWrite returns 200, one journal entry is pushed, and the rendered order is unchanged. src/app carries 4 such conditional-render sites today. Pre-mortem S3 states the risk in the opposite direction and routes surfacing to EG-1, whose stop trigger requires the panel to report the arrows as REFUSED — but here they are enabled, so EG-1 as specified cannot produce its own trigger. Acceptance 22 checks git diff only on a refused drag.
impact: The feature's correctness core — the blue line's slot is the slot the write produces — is asserted by no gate, and the failure mode is a silent successful write that moves nothing rather than a refusal the user can read. It also makes DR47-6's partial-move policy unsafe in the same class: only no-adjacent-sibling is treated as overshoot, and a hidden but admissible op-unit produces no refusal at all.
required_correction: (1) Make the slot-to-op-unit correspondence a precondition of the gesture rather than a post-hoc residual: the client already holds parentOid / prevOid / nextOid per element, so the eligibility predicate can require each DOM slot's neighbour oids to match the engine's baseline neighbours and refuse the parent on mismatch. Promote this into DR47-7 with its own Korean refusal string and RED-when, or state explicitly why it is not required. (2) Add an end-to-end acceptance criterion that after a committed n-step drag the target's index among its parent's rendered children equals the index the insertion line displayed, with a RED-when that makes it fail. (3) Restate EG-1's evidence method so it measures the slot-count versus op-unit-count disagreement per parent.

claim: DR47-7's drop-index contract derives the slot list from DOM element children alone while the engine already publishes its own source op-unit neighbour chain, which the plan neither cites nor uses; the mismatch the plan names as its central risk is routed to EG-1, whose stated measurement cannot observe it.
evidence: edit-map.ts emits prevOid / nextOid / parentOid per oid, and adjacentOpUnit's docblock states it is the ONE function computing both the D7 baseline neighbours and the move swap partner — the artifact already carries the engine's source-order sibling chain, computed by the same code the write uses. edit-map.ts also emits opUnitKind?: 'conditional-container'. A grep for prevOid, nextOid, parentOid, edit-map and opUnitKind over the plan returns nothing. Pre-mortem S3 says 'Prevented by: nothing structural' and names no channel for its mitigation. EG-1's only mismatch trigger fires when the panel reports the arrows as refused, which is silent on the case where the engine is eligible but its op-unit population differs in length or ordering from the geometric slot list. That case is live in this corpus: KI-10 shared-oid means one source op-unit routinely renders k DOM siblings, and opUnitElement admits containers that render zero.
impact: The blue line's slot index maps to the step count n for DR47-6's fold. Where the two populations diverge n is wrong, and the outcomes are not refusals: a .map()-rendered list under a heading gives move-up a legitimate swap partner, so the user drags one card one slot and the source moves the whole list. Nothing in acceptance 19-23 compares the post-write source order against the promised slot, and the partial-move policy compounds it — a step-count mismatch surfacing as no-adjacent-sibling at step k>1 is indistinguishable from a genuine overshoot and is silently committed as a partial move. This is a scope and acceptance-semantics change, not polish.
required_correction: (1) Make reconciliation between the geometric slot list and the engine's prevOid/nextOid chain a mandatory part of DR47-7's predicate and an S47-1 acceptance criterion with its own RED-when, not an S47-3 contingency. (2) Rule explicitly what the gesture does when the chains disagree in length or order, with a refusal string that does not claim 'no sibling' to a user looking at four. (3) Extend EG-1 to report, per eligible parent, geometric slot count versus engine op-unit count and their orderings, so the stated stop boundary is reachable. (4) Re-rule the partial-move policy so a clamped commit is only permitted when the drop slot is at the visible end of a reconciled list, never as the fallback for a mid-list refusal.

claim: Acceptance 21 and EG-2's pass path compare the fold to itself, so the phase's only correctness gate on the fold's output bytes cannot go RED, and it carries no RED-when while its siblings 19, 20 and 22 do.
evidence: Section 3.6 rules the fold is repeated application of the shipped pure function, n in-memory parses. The assertion the plan writes has the same call sequence on both sides of the equality, with expect on step 1 on both sides. EG-2's claim is stated against n sequential single-step WRITES, but its evidence method substitutes the pure composition for the write path, which is strictly weaker and self-satisfying. The internal tell is EG-2's alternate path, which presupposes the two sides can differ in whitespace — they cannot if they are the same expression. moveAdjacent re-parses and re-validates per call, so step 2+ risk is real but identical on both sides and therefore invisible to the comparison; only EG-2's unexpected-result clause observes anything.
impact: S47-4 is gated on EG-2 having answered, and acceptance 21 is promoted to a permanent unit gate. Nothing else in 19-23 checks that a folded n-step drag produces the same source order as n discrete moves: 19 counts journal entries, 20 checks one Cmd+Z restores the pre-drag bytes (true even if the drag wrote the wrong order), 22 covers refusals. Approving this ships the write half with its output-correctness gate being scaffolding.
required_correction: Restate EG-2's subject as the sidecar path — one folded POST versus n sequential POSTs, compared on the on-disk page.tsx bytes after each — so the two sides run different code, and give acceptance 21 an explicit RED-when (for example hoist span resolution out of the loop so steps 2..n reuse step 1's spans, which must then make the fold diverge from the sequential result). Alternatively replace 21 with an independent oracle on the resulting source order and state its mutation.
